goals: Mechanistic: characterize day-of-year of snowmelt onset as a function of elevation across the Naches
Validation: compare simulated SWE and melt timing to the 6 SNOTEL stations (co-located)
Requested sub-goal: resolve the local lapse rate between individual stations on the same ridge (<12 km apart)
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (acting through forcing temperature/precip and melt energy)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates snow/SWE and melt (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT, SNOW) in default output; SNOTEL provides co-located SWE validation. Snow is a fast state, so heavy spin-up is unnecessary.

answerable: Broad-scale elevation control on snowmelt-onset timing across the basin, sampled across DISTINCT (>12 km separated) NLDAS-2 cells so that forcing temperature/precip genuinely differ
Co-located SNOTEL SWE / melt-out validation at each station's 12 km cell (with expected ridgetop SWE underestimation)

not_answerable.aspect: Local lapse rate between individual SNOTEL stations on the same ridge (<12 km apart)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 forcing is 0.125° (~12 km) with no within-cell lapse rate; sub-12 km stations frequently fall in the same forcing cell and receive identical T/precip, so any inter-station melt-timing difference is a grid artifact, not a resolved lapse rate
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled / sub-12 km forcing with an explicit lapse rate

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation, with validation columns pinned to observation sites
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Four elevation bands x ~2 columns per band placed in DISTINCT NLDAS cells to trace the resolvable melt-onset-vs-elevation gradient. The ~1625 m relief supports ~15 distinct NLDAS precip values, so ~8 well-separated columns span the gradient without redundancy; more would sample the same forcing cells and add no independent information.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the rain-snow transition (750-1200 m) where melt-onset sensitivity to elevation is steepest, and place columns in SEPARATE NLDAS cells so their forcing actually differs; avoid clustering multiple exploratory columns inside one 12 km cell.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light: ~2 per band across different cells to check gradient robustness, not within-cell replication (which would be identical forcing).

sampling_plan.reason: Anchors the warm, low end of the elevation-melt-timing gradient (little/no persistent snow).
Steepest sensitivity of melt-onset to elevation; oversampled to resolve the gradient's inflection.
Mid-high band where a coherent snowpack forms; traces melt onset shift with elevation.
Cold end of the gradient; expected latest melt onset (subject to 12 km SWE underestimation).
Pinned to the 6 SNOTEL stations for co-located SWE / melt validation; stations sharing a NLDAS cell are NOT independent forcing samples.

validation_design.target_variable: peak_SWE and snowmelt-out date (from H2OSNO / QSNOMELT)
validation_design.comparison: co-located — each SNOTEL matched to its nearest NLDAS/soil column; note stations <12 km apart share a forcing cell and cannot be independently distinguished
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE on peak SWE; day-of-year error on melt onset/melt-out
validation_design.n_validation_points: 6 (fewer independent forcing samples where stations co-occupy a cell)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (default), native SSURGO soil, ~2-3 spin-up years, multi-year climatological averaging of melt onset

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled / sub-12 km forcing with explicit lapse rate
requires_capabilities.why: Stations <12 km apart share one NLDAS cell and get identical T/precip
requires_capabilities.blocks: Resolving the local lapse rate between individual same-ridge SNOTEL stations (the headline request)

requires_capabilities.capability: snowmelt-onset diagnostic (day-of-year from QSNOMELT / H2OSNO decline)
requires_capabilities.why: Onset date must be derived from the snow time series
requires_capabilities.blocks: Quantitative melt-onset comparison and gradient fitting

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + NLDAS-cell resolver to guarantee exploratory columns fall in DISTINCT forcing cells
requires_capabilities.why: Stratifying by elevation only helps if columns occupy different forcing cells

assumptions: Snowmelt onset can be defined operationally from QSNOMELT onset / start of sustained H2OSNO decline.
Snow is a fast state; ~2-3 spin-up years suffice, no multi-year groundwater spin-up needed.
Averaging over multiple forcing years (within 1980-2018) yields a climatological elevation-melt relationship rather than single-year noise.
Ridgetop SWE will be underestimated because 12 km NLDAS cells average over terrain.
open_questions: Which of the 6 SNOTEL stations actually fall within the same NLDAS 0.125° cell? (Determines how many are independent forcing samples.)
Is a future elevation-downscaled forcing product (e.g. lapse-rate-corrected or ParFlow-CONUS2-informed) planned, since it is required for the same-ridge lapse-rate goal?
Preferred melt-onset definition/threshold, and single vs multi-year climatology window?
